title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon-Garlic Butter Sauce
description: Crisp-skinned salmon fillets finished with a quick pan sauce of garlic, lemon, and butter. One skillet and about 25 minutes from start to finish.
notes: Timing is for fillets 1 to 1 1/4 inches thick at the thickest point; thinner tail pieces need 1 to 2 minutes less on the skin side. Dry skin is what makes it crisp, so do not skip patting the fish dry. Skinless fillets work too: sear 4 minutes on the first side and 3 to 4 on the second. Dry white wine can replace the broth. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days; leftover salmon is best cold or gently flaked into rice or salad rather than reheated hard.

ingredients.name: skin-on salmon fillets, about 6 oz each and 1 to 1 1/4 inches thick
avocado oil or other high-heat neutral oil
cold unsalted butter, cut into 3 pieces
fresh lemon juice, from about 1 lemon

instructions: Pat the salmon very dry on all sides with paper towels, especially the skin. Let it sit at room temperature for 10 minutes, then season the flesh and skin with the 3/4 teaspoon salt and the pepper.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, about 2 minutes. Lay the fillets in skin side down, placing them away from you, and press each one flat with a spatula for 10 seconds so the skin stays in contact with the pan.
Reduce the heat to medium and cook without moving for 6 to 7 minutes, until the skin is crisp and releases easily and the flesh has turned opaque about three-quarters of the way up the sides.
Flip the fillets and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the thickest part reads 145°F on an instant-read thermometer, or the flesh is opaque and flakes when pressed. Transfer to plates, skin side up.

Pour off all but a thin film of fat and let the pan cool off the heat for 1 minute. Return it to medium-low heat, add 1 piece of butter and the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the broth and lemon juice, raise the heat to medium, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the liquid is reduced by about half.

Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the remaining 2 pieces of butter until the sauce looks glossy. Stir in the parsley and the pinch of salt, then spoon the sauce around the salmon rather than over the skin, so the skin stays crisp.

title: Thai-Style Basil Shrimp
description: Shrimp stir-fried over high heat with garlic, chiles, and a savory sauce, then tossed with a big handful of basil. Modeled on pad kra pao and ready faster than the rice it is served on.
notes: Start the rice before you prep; the stir-fry itself takes about 5 minutes. Holy basil is traditional, Thai basil is easier to find, and Italian basil still makes a good dish. Two chiles gives medium heat; use one seeded serrano for mild. There is no added salt because the oyster sauce, soy sauce, and fish sauce season the dish. A crisp fried egg on top is traditional but adds egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour. Reheat briefly so the shrimp do not turn rubbery.

ingredients.name: large shrimp (21 to 25 per pound), peeled, deveined, and patted dry
Thai bird's eye chiles, thinly sliced, or 1 serrano
green beans, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
loosely packed Thai basil or holy basil leaves
hot steamed jasmine rice, for serving

instructions: Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and water together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Set every prepped ingredient next to the stove; the cooking moves quickly.

Heat a wok or 12-inch skillet over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until a drop of water evaporates on contact. Add the oil, then the garlic, chiles, and shallot, and stir-fry for 20 to 30 seconds, until fragrant and just turning golden.
Add the green beans and stir-fry for 1 minute, until bright green.
Spread the shrimp in a single layer and let them sear undisturbed for 1 minute, then stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes, until mostly pink with a little gray remaining.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 30 to 60 seconds, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through, curled into a loose C, and coated in a light glaze.
Take the pan off the heat, add the basil, and toss for about 15 seconds, until just wilted. Serve right away over the rice.

title: Kerala-Style Coconut Fish Curry
description: Chunks of white fish simmered gently in a turmeric-gold coconut sauce with mustard seeds, ginger, and tomato. Mildly spicy, dairy-free, and made for spooning over rice.
equipment: wide deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid
notes: Use any firm white fish about 1 inch thick: cod, halibut, haddock, or mahi-mahi. Thinner fillets such as tilapia need only 4 to 5 minutes. Contains coconut and mustard seeds. If you cannot find Kashmiri chili powder, use 3/4 teaspoon sweet paprika plus 1/4 teaspoon cayenne. The sauce can be made a day ahead and refrigerated; bring it back to a simmer and cook the fish just before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating gently so the fish does not break up. Refrigerate any leftover rice within 1 hour.

ingredients.name: skinless cod or halibut fillets, about 1 inch thick, cut into 2-inch pieces

instructions: Toss the fish with 3/4 teaspoon of the salt and 1/4 teaspoon of the turmeric. Set aside at room temperature while you make the sauce, no longer than 20 minutes.

Heat the oil in a wide, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cook for 30 to 60 seconds, until they begin to pop. Add the curry leaves if using (they will spatter), then the onion and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring often, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the onion is soft and golden at the edges.
Add the ginger, garlic, and serrano and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. Stir in the coriander, chili powder, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon turmeric and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they collapse into a thick paste and the oil glistens at the edges.
Pour in the coconut milk and water and bring to a gentle simmer. Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.

Nestle the fish into the sauce in a single layer and spoon some sauce over the top. Cover and simmer gently over medium-low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, swirling the pan instead of stirring, until the fish is opaque throughout and flakes easily, or reads 145°F in the thickest piece.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice, taking care not to break the fish. Let the curry rest for 5 minutes, then serve with steamed rice.

title: Korean-Style Tuna Mayo Rice Bowls
description: A pantry dinner based on chamchi mayo deopbap: warm rice topped with soy-glazed canned tuna, soft scrambled eggs, roasted seaweed, and a drizzle of mayonnaise. No raw fish involved.
notes: The water amount is for rinsed, well-drained short-grain rice on the stovetop; in a rice cooker, follow the cooker's line for white rice. Kewpie-style mayonnaise is the classic choice, but any mayonnaise works. Either oil-packed or water-packed tuna is fine as long as it is drained well. For heat, stir a little gochujang into the mayonnaise. Use gluten-free tamari in place of soy sauce to avoid wheat. Refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour and the tuna and eggs within 2 hours; eat within 2 days and reheat the rice until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: roasted seasoned seaweed (gim), crumbled or cut into strips

instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl with several changes of cold water, swishing with your hand, until the water is mostly clear. Drain well in a fine sieve.

Combine the rice and the 1 3/4 cups water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then cover tightly, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 13 minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand, still covered, for 10 minutes, until the grains are tender and glossy. Fluff with a rice paddle or fork.

While the rice rests, beat the eggs with the salt. Heat half of the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat, add the eggs, and stir slowly for 1 to 2 minutes, until they form soft curds with no liquid egg remaining. Transfer to a plate.
Wipe out the skillet, add the remaining oil, and set over medium heat. Cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft and translucent.

Add the tuna, breaking it into chunks, along with the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the tuna is hot throughout. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame oil.

Divide the rice among 4 bowls. Top with the tuna, eggs, and cucumber, drizzle each bowl with about 1 tablespoon mayonnaise, and finish with the seaweed, scallions, and sesame seeds. Mix everything together before eating.

title: Weeknight Shrimp Paella-Style Skillet Rice
description: Short-grain rice simmered in a smoky tomato and paprika base, topped with shrimp and peas and left unstirred so the bottom toasts. A skillet take on Spanish paella that works on a regular stove burner.
notes: Rice and liquid: the 4 cups of broth are for Spanish bomba or Calasparra rice, which absorbs more than other rices. If using Arborio, reduce the broth to 3 1/2 cups and start checking the rice after 12 minutes of simmering. Do not rinse the rice and do not stir once it simmers; stirring makes it creamy like risotto instead of separate and toasty. If your burner is smaller than the pan, shift the skillet every few minutes so the rice cooks evenly. The salt amount assumes low-sodium broth; with regular broth, cut the salt added with the broth to 1/2 teaspoon. Naturally gluten-free if your broth is. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour because of the rice, eat within 2 days, and reheat until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: large shrimp (21 to 25 per pound), peeled and deveined
red bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice
bomba or Calasparra rice (or Arborio; see notes)

instructions: Toss the shrimp with 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, 1/2 teaspoon of the smoked paprika, and 1 tablespoon of the oil; refrigerate until needed. Warm the broth with the saffron in a small saucepan over medium heat until steaming, then keep it on low.
Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft but not browned.
Stir in the garlic and the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons paprika for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the mixture is thick, jammy, and a shade darker.

Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat the grains. Pour in the warm broth and the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, stir once to spread the rice in an even layer, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

Reduce the heat to medium-low to hold a steady simmer and cook uncovered, without stirring, for 15 minutes, rotating the pan now and then, until most of the liquid is absorbed and the rice at the surface is nearly tender.

Scatter the peas over the top and press the shrimp into the rice in a single layer. Cook for 4 minutes, turn the shrimp over, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the shrimp are pink and opaque throughout and no liquid pools when you tilt the pan.
For a toasted bottom layer, raise the heat to medium-high for 60 to 90 seconds, until you hear the rice crackle and smell toasting, then stop before it smells burnt.
Remove from the heat, cover with foil or a lid, and rest for 5 minutes so the rice finishes steaming. Sprinkle with the parsley and serve from the pan with lemon wedges.

title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Garlic and Herbs
description: Small potatoes boiled until tender, flattened, and roasted in olive oil until the edges shatter, then finished with garlic, parsley, and lemon zest.
notes: Choose potatoes of similar size so they cook evenly; larger ones can be halved after boiling. Letting the boiled potatoes steam dry is what allows them to crisp, so do not rush that step. Do not line the pan with parchment at this temperature; bare metal browns better, and a thin metal spatula will release the potatoes. Make ahead: boil and smash the potatoes up to a day in advance, refrigerate uncovered on the pan, and add 5 minutes to the roasting time. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated; re-crisp at 425°F for 10 minutes rather than microwaving.

ingredients.name: baby yellow or gold potatoes, about 1 1/2 inches wide, scrubbed
fine sea salt, for the cooking water

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the lower-middle position. Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with about 2 quarts of cold water, and add the 1 tablespoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer and cook for 18 to 22 minutes, until a paring knife slides into the center with no resistance.
Drain the potatoes in a colander and let them steam dry for 5 minutes, until the skins look matte.

Spread 2 tablespoons of the oil over a rimmed baking sheet. Arrange the potatoes on the sheet with space between them and press each one with the bottom of a glass or measuring cup until about 1/2 inch thick, with ragged edges.
Drizzle 1 tablespoon of the oil over the tops and season with the 3/4 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Roast for 25 minutes, until the undersides are deep golden brown.

Flip the potatoes with a thin metal spatula. Stir the garlic into the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and dab it over the potatoes, then roast for 10 to 12 minutes more, until both sides are crisp and the garlic is pale gold, not dark brown.
Sprinkle with the parsley and lemon zest and serve hot, straight from the pan.

title: French-Style Lentil Salad with Dijon Vinaigrette
description: Small green lentils dressed while warm with a sharp mustard and shallot vinaigrette, then tossed with finely diced carrot, celery, and parsley. Gluten-free, and it tastes better on the second day.
notes: Gluten-free as written. Lentils are often processed alongside wheat and barley, so pick them over, rinse well, and buy lentils labeled gluten-free if cooking for someone with celiac disease; check the mustard label as well. Contains mustard. Use French green (du Puy) or black beluga lentils, which hold their shape; ordinary brown lentils work but turn soft, so check them at 15 minutes, and red lentils will not work. Keeps 5 days refrigerated in a covered container. The lentils absorb dressing as they sit, so refresh leftovers with a splash of vinegar and a pinch of salt, and serve at room temperature.

ingredients.name: French green (du Puy) lentils, picked over and rinsed
fine sea salt, for the cooking water
medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice

instructions: Combine the lentils, water, bay leaf, garlic, and the 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender all the way through but still hold their shape. Start tasting at 18 minutes.

While the lentils cook, stir the shallot, vinegar, and the 3/4 teaspoon salt together in a large bowl and let stand for 10 minutes to soften the shallot's bite. Whisk in the mustard and pepper, then the olive oil, until the dressing thickens slightly.

Drain the lentils well in a fine-mesh sieve and discard the bay leaf and garlic. Add the warm lentils to the bowl and fold gently until coated; warm lentils absorb the dressing far better than cold ones.
Let the lentils cool for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, then fold in the carrots, celery, and parsley.
Taste and adjust with a little more vinegar or a pinch of salt if the salad tastes flat. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Smashed Cucumber Salad with Garlic and Sesame
description: Cucumbers cracked open so their rough edges soak up a dressing of soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, and toasted sesame oil. Cold, crunchy, and good next to anything rich or spicy.
notes: Contains sesame and soy; the soy sauce also contains wheat. For a gluten-free version, use gluten-free tamari. The prep time includes 15 minutes of draining, which keeps the dressing from being watered down. Thin-skinned Persian or English cucumbers work best; if using regular slicing cucumbers, peel them and scoop out the seeds. Chinese black vinegar can replace the rice vinegar for a deeper flavor. Best within an hour of dressing; leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated but soften and release liquid.

ingredients.name: Persian cucumbers (about 6) or 1 large English cucumber

instructions: Trim the ends of the cucumbers. Lay each one on a cutting board and press down firmly with the flat side of a chef's knife, or tap with a rolling pin, until it cracks and splits lengthwise. Cut or tear the pieces into rough 1-inch chunks.
Toss the cucumbers in a colander with the salt and 1/2 teaspoon of the sugar. Set over a bowl or the sink and let drain for 15 minutes, until a few tablespoons of liquid have collected.
Meanwhile, whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, red pepper flakes, and remaining 1 teaspoon sugar in a mixing bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Shake the colander well and pat the cucumbers dry with a clean towel; do not rinse them. Add them to the bowl and toss until evenly coated.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and the cilantro if using. Serve right away, or chill for up to 30 minutes for a colder, more seasoned salad.

title: Roasted Broccoli with Garlic and Lemon
description: Broccoli roasted on a preheated pan until the stems are tender and the edges are deeply browned, with sliced garlic added partway so it turns golden instead of bitter.
notes: Dry the broccoli thoroughly after washing; wet florets steam instead of browning. Cutting florets so each has one flat side gives more contact with the hot pan. Do not crowd the pan: if doubling, use two sheets and swap their positions halfway through. The peeled stems are sweet and worth roasting along with the florets. Leftovers keep 4 days refrigerated and are good cold in grain bowls or reheated in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes.

ingredients.name: broccoli (about 2 medium heads), cut into 1 1/2-inch florets, stems peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick

instructions: Place a rimmed baking sheet on the lower-middle oven rack and heat the oven to 425°F, letting the pan heat with it for at least 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, toss the broccoli florets and stems with 2 1/2 tablespoons of the oil, the salt, and the pepper until evenly coated. Keep the bowl handy for the garlic.
Carefully spread the broccoli on the hot pan in a single layer with the flat cut sides down. Roast for 12 minutes, until the undersides are well browned.

Toss the garlic and red pepper flakes with the remaining 1/2 tablespoon oil. Scatter them over the broccoli, stir, and roast for 8 to 10 minutes more, until the stems are tender when pierced with a knife, the floret tips are dark and crisp, and the garlic is golden.
Sprinkle the lemon zest over the broccoli and squeeze on the juice of half the lemon, about 1 tablespoon. Toss on the pan, taste, add more lemon if you like, and serve hot or warm.

title: Jollof-Style Rice
description: Long-grain rice steamed in a fried-down base of tomato, red bell pepper, and Scotch bonnet with thyme and curry powder, in the style of Nigerian party jollof. Smoky-sweet, brick red, and a natural partner for grilled or roasted mains.
equipment: Dutch oven or heavy pot with tight lid
notes: Rice and liquid: this ratio is for long-grain parboiled (converted) rice, which stays separate and resists turning mushy. The rice cooks in the reduced pepper base plus 2 cups of broth, so reducing the base until thick matters as much as measuring the broth. If using basmati instead, cut the broth to 1 1/2 cups and the covered cooking time to 20 minutes total. A whole Scotch bonnet makes this properly hot; seed it or use half for medium heat. The salt amount assumes low-sodium broth; with regular broth, use 1 teaspoon. Naturally gluten-free if your broth and curry powder are. A lightly toasted layer at the bottom of the pot is prized, not a mistake. Cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; eat within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: diced tomatoes (14.5 oz), with their juices
large red bell pepper, seeded and roughly chopped
medium yellow onion, half roughly chopped and half thinly sliced
Scotch bonnet or habanero chile, stemmed (seeded for less heat)
long-grain parboiled (converted) rice, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear and drained

instructions: Blend the tomatoes with their juices, the bell pepper, the roughly chopped half of the onion, the chile, garlic, and ginger until completely smooth, about 1 minute. You should have about 3 cups.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden at the edges.
Add the tomato paste and fry, stirring constantly, for 2 to 3 minutes, until it darkens from bright red to brick red and smells sweet.

Pour in the blended pepper base carefully, as it will spatter. Stir in the curry powder, thyme, smoked paprika, bay leaves, and salt. Cook, partially covered and stirring every few minutes, for 12 to 15 minutes, until the sauce has reduced by about a third, looks thick, and oil pools at the edges.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Stir in the rinsed rice until every grain is coated and the surface is level.
Cover the pot with a sheet of foil, press the lid on tightly over it, and reduce the heat to the lowest setting. Cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.

Uncover and gently turn the rice from the bottom with a fork or wooden spoon. Re-cover with the foil and lid and cook for 10 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. If the rice is still firm and the pot is dry, sprinkle in 1/4 cup water, cover, and cook 5 minutes longer.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Discard the bay leaves, fluff with a fork, and serve.
